 INJURY REPORT  
 With Saturday's 7:30 p.m. kickoff approaching, the ACC has released its availability report for Pitt's matchup with Georgia Tech. The Panthers will be without two contributors, and a third is up in the air.
 OUT
 LB Cam Lindsey 
Lindsey misses his first game of the season after Pat Narduzzi ruled him out for the year earlier this week. He had played in all eight games and has six tackles, serving as a key depth piece.
 DT Eliyt Nairne 
Nairne is not a starter, but he has seen a good amount of reps. He has played in seven games this season with six tackles and half a sack. His absence thins out a defensive line that is already light on depth.
 GAME TIME DECISION
 RB Ja'Kyrian Turner 
Turner has appeared in three games this season, rushing 30 times for 3.7 yards per carry and a touchdown. He has not played since North Carolina, missing Boston College and Miami.
 GOOD NEWS
 RB Damon Ferguson Jr. 
Ferguson was on an availability report earlier this week but is not listed today, meaning he is available. That is big news, especially if Turner can't go. He leads the team with 477 rushing yards on 92 carries, averaging 5.2 yards per carry with four touchdowns.
 TRAILER: PITT VS. GEORGIA TECH 
 THE SCRIPT: PITT VS. GEORGIA TECH 
 PREVIEW 
 The Pitt Panthers (5-3, 2-3 ACC) host Georgia Tech (2-5, 1-3 ACC) in primetime this Saturday at 7:30 PM on ESPN2. 
 Pitt and Georgia Tech meet for the 19th time in a series that dates to 1918. The Panthers lead the all-time series, 12-6, and have won seven of the past nine meetings. Pitt owns a 5-2 series record in Pittsburgh. 
 The Panthers defeated then No. 15 ranked Georgia Tech, 42-28, in Atlanta last season. Pitt has won five of the past six meetings and leads the ACC series, 7-4. 
 This Saturday's game against Georgia Tech will feature Hail to Heroes, sponsored by GBU Life and the Aldrich Foundation, honoring military members, veterans and first responders through on-field and in-game recognitions and patriotic elements celebrating those who serve. As part of their sponsorship, GBU Life and the Aldrich Foundation will sponsor the on-field and in-game recognition of heroes and veterans. Both organizations share a commitment to supporting active-duty personnel, veterans and their families, turning appreciation into action through GBU Life's Operation Reach Out, which delivers care packages to deployed service members, and the Aldrich Foundation's support of organizations such as Wreaths Across America and Joint Task Force K9s. Together, they help bring the community together to recognize service and make a lasting impact on those who have sacrificed for our country.
